title: M0 language decision
summary: This report applies the decision rule registered before benchmarking. Hard gates determine eligibility; weighted scores rank eligible candidates.

decision.title: Decision: Rust
decision.detail: Rust is selected by the locked M0 rule: it passes the required target and black-box parity gates and scores 84.09/100 versus Go at 67.21/100, a 16.88-point lead. Go is faster in this HTTP workload and in clean builds. The result applies to the tested Feluka scope and does not certify a complete production application.

sections.title: Weighted score
sections.description: Each category score is multiplied by its registered weight, then added to produce the final score out of 100.

metrics.label: Overall
metrics.explanation: Weighted total = sum(category score × category weight). The weights were fixed before the final measurement runs; see the score-by-criterion section for each measured input and calculation.

sections.title: Score by criterion
sections.description: Each row shows a category score out of 100 and its separate weight in the final score. Hover or focus a category name for the measured inputs and exact scoring rule. These scores do not override a failed hard gate.

metrics.label: Target coverage
metrics.weight_explanation: Why 20%? The M0 preregistration assigned this share before the final measurements, so this criterion can add at most 20 of the total 100 points. Its contribution is category score × 20 ÷ 100. The preregistration records the chosen weight but does not give a separate rationale for its relative size compared with the other criteria; this report preserves the fixed choice rather than inventing a post-hoc reason. See docs/PREREGISTRATION.md.
metrics.explanation:
Score = required target classes passed ÷ 5 × 100. Each class counts equally; this is coverage, not a speed score.
Rust: 5/5 classes passed (server linux x86 64, browser wasm, desktop, mobile android, no std bare metal).
Go: 5/5 classes passed (server linux x86 64, browser wasm, desktop, mobile android, tinygo mcu).
Weight in final score: 20%.

metrics.explanation:
Score is the unweighted mean of four subscores: paired elapsed-time estimate, source lines, edit/test iterations to first green, and unexpected failing test runs. For the last three, fewer is better and the score is 100 × best observed value ÷ candidate value. Both languages receive 100 for elapsed time because they were implemented in one paired task and cannot be timed separately.
Rust: 223 source lines (subscore 100.00), 1 iteration(s) (subscore 100.00), 0 unexpected failing run(s) (subscore 100.00); mean = 100.00/100.
Go: 270 source lines (subscore 82.59), 2 iteration(s) (subscore 50.00), 1 unexpected failing run(s) (subscore 0.00); mean = 58.15/100.
Weight in final score: 20%.

metrics.weight_explanation: Why 15%? The M0 preregistration assigned this share before the final measurements, so this criterion can add at most 15 of the total 100 points. Its contribution is category score × 15 ÷ 100. The preregistration records the chosen weight but does not give a separate rationale for its relative size compared with the other criteria; this report preserves the fixed choice rather than inventing a post-hoc reason. metrics.explanation:
Score = properties passed ÷ 5 × 100. The five checks cover explicit missing-value handling, whether the compiler forces that handling, explicit parser errors, whether the compiler forces error handling, and fail-closed behavior for invalid rules.
Both languages pass 3/5: they represent missing values and parser errors explicitly and reject malformed/unknown rules, but neither compiler forces callers to handle missing values or parser errors. That is 3 ÷ 5 × 100 = 60/100 for each.
Weight in final score: 15%.

metrics.explanation:
Score (0–100; higher is better). This uses median server processing time from three runs at concurrency 1, not browser/client request time.
Formula: 50 × max(0, 1 − p50 / 1 ms) + 50 × max(0, 1 − p99 / 5 ms).
Rust: p50 0.278 ms and p99 0.519 ms → 50 × 0.7220 + 50 × 0.8962 = 36.10 + 44.81 = 80.91/100.
Go: p50 0.211 ms and p99 0.444 ms → 50 × 0.7890 + 50 × 0.9112 = 39.45 + 45.56 = 85.01/100.
Go scores higher on this criterion. Weighted contribution: Rust 12.14 points; Go 12.75 points. Weight in final score: 15%.

metrics.explanation:
Score is the mean of two inverse-ratio scores: clean build and source-edit rebuild. For each, score = 100 × fastest measured time ÷ this language’s time; lower build time is better. No-op build time was measured but is not included in this score.
Rust: clean 59.56 s (subscore 43.49); edit rebuild 8.16 s (subscore 15.60); mean = 29.54/100.
Go: clean 25.90 s (subscore 100.00); edit rebuild 1.27 s (subscore 100.00); mean = 100.00/100.
Weight in final score: 10%.

sections.title: Scope and limits
sections.text: The result covers the measured M0 scenario and frozen record-rule subset. It does not claim full PocketBase filter compatibility or certify production performance for a complete application.

limitations: The result applies to the preregistered M0 scope and its measured workloads.
